chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Kufi from Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Sufyan from Amr ibn Hurayth who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Say in the first two rak'ahs, after the Tashahhud and before rising - Subhanallah, Subhanallah, seven times.'
ai.seo_question: What specific dhikr should be recited seven times after Tashahhud in the first two rak'ahs of prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs the narrator to recite 'Subhanallah' seven times in each of the first two rak'ahs of the prayer, specifically after the Tashahhud and before standing up for the next rak'ah. This establishes a specific recommended supplication (du'a) and dhikr practice within the ritual prayer structure, reflecting the Shia emphasis on detailed devotional acts (mustahabbat) that enhance spiritual presence (khushu) during Salah. The practice underscores the tradition of transmitting precise liturgical instructions through reliable chains of narrators, as seen in Shaykh al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
